description: Systematic software testing and quality assurance: testing fundamentals and the test pyramid, black-box and white-box test design, coverage criteria, unit, integration and end-to-end testing, test-driven development, performance and security testing, and quality metrics and process improvement. Students write and run real test suites against seeded-fault programs in the browser, measuring coverage and mutation scores to see which of their tests actually find bugs.
modelledOn: Ammann and Offutt, Introduction to Software Testing
Myers, Badgett and Sandler, The Art of Software Testing
ISTQB Certified Tester Foundation Level syllabus
outcomes: Explain the vocabulary and principles of testing and plan a test strategy using the test pyramid and risk.
Design black-box tests with equivalence partitioning, boundary values, decision tables, state transitions and combinatorial methods.
Measure and improve white-box coverage, including branch, MC/DC and data-flow coverage, and assess test quality by mutation analysis.
Write maintainable unit, integration and end-to-end tests with test doubles, and develop code test-first.
Plan and run performance and security tests and interpret their results.
Use quality metrics, reviews and process models to assess and improve software quality.

units.title: Testing fundamentals and the test pyramid
topics: Errors, faults and failures; testing versus debugging; verification and validation
The test oracle problem; the principles of testing; why exhaustive testing is impossible
Test levels and test types; static and dynamic testing
The test pyramid and its alternatives; the cost of finding defects late
Famous failures and what testing would have caught

units.title: Black-box test design
topics: Equivalence partitioning and boundary value analysis
Decision tables and cause-effect graphing
State transition testing
Combinatorial and pairwise testing; covering arrays
Use-case-based, error-guessing and exploratory testing
Worked example: testing mobile money transfer limits, fee bands and reversals

units.title: White-box testing and coverage
topics: Control-flow graphs; statement, branch and condition coverage
Modified condition/decision coverage and where it is required
Basis-path testing and cyclomatic complexity
Data-flow testing: definitions, uses and def-use paths
Mutation testing: mutation operators, mutation score and equivalent mutants
Coverage tools and the limits of coverage as a goal

units.title: Unit, integration and end-to-end tests
topics: Unit testing frameworks; arrange-act-assert, fixtures and parameterised tests
Test doubles: dummies, stubs, fakes, spies and mocks; when mocking hurts
Integration strategies: big bang, top-down, bottom-up and sandwich; testing against real databases in containers
Contract testing between services
End-to-end browser testing; flaky tests and how to fix them
Testing under simulated slow and unreliable 2G and 3G networks

units.title: Test-driven development
topics: The red-green-refactor cycle; katas and worked examples
Behaviour-driven development with Gherkin scenarios
Property-based testing and generators
Characterisation tests for legacy code without tests
Evidence on the costs and benefits of TDD

units.title: Performance and security testing
topics: Load, stress, soak and spike testing; workload models
Performance metrics: latency percentiles, throughput, error rates and resource utilisation
Capacity testing for month-end salary peaks on a payment service
Security testing: static and dynamic analysis, fuzzing and penetration testing basics
The OWASP Web Security Testing Guide
Reporting performance and security findings

units.title: Test management and automation
topics: Test plans and strategies; risk-based testing and entry and exit criteria
The defect life cycle and writing good bug reports
Continuous integration pipelines and automated regression suites; regression test selection
Test environments, test data management and data privacy

units.title: Quality metrics and process improvement
topics: Software quality models: ISO/IEC 25010 characteristics
Product metrics: defect density, escaped defects, complexity, code churn
Reliability: failure intensity, MTTF and reliability growth models
Reviews and inspections; static analysis and linters in the pipeline
Process improvement: CMMI, ISO 9001, retrospectives and root-cause analysis
Delivery metrics: deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate and time to restore

units.title: Testing for real users
topics: Usability and accessibility testing
Localisation testing for local languages, number and currency formats
Mobile testing across low-end devices and Android versions
Capstone: a complete test suite and quality report for a seeded-fault application

schedule.title: Why and what we test
schedule.exercise: Pick a famous software failure, state the fault, the error and the failure and say which test level could have caught it.

tasks.title: Run a buggy discount function, identify the fault, the error state and the visible failure, then fix it and rerun the test
Write a test oracle for a sorting function using properties and a trusted reference, and run it on 10 inputs including an empty list
Estimate how many tests exist at unit, service and UI levels for a given project, time each level and propose a better balance

schedule.title: Black-box test design
schedule.exercise: Design test cases for a grade-to-letter function using equivalence classes and boundaries, and count the cases you need.

tasks.title: Derive equivalence classes and boundary values for an age-based ticket price function and run the resulting tests, reporting any failures
Build a decision table for a loan eligibility rule with four conditions, reduce redundant rules and write a test for each remaining rule
Draw a state machine for an ATM session, derive tests covering all transitions and find an invalid transition the code wrongly allows

schedule.title: Combinatorial and experience-based testing
schedule.exercise: Test mobile money limits by listing fee bands, daily caps and reversal rules, and show your boundary tests for each.

tasks.title: Generate a pairwise test set for four parameters with three values each and compare its size with the 81 exhaustive combinations
Run a timed exploratory session on a seeded checkout function, log the charter and findings and classify each defect
Write a test suite for a transfer function with limits, fee bands and reversals, and find at least four seeded defects with it

schedule.title: Structural coverage
schedule.exercise: Draw the control-flow graph of a function with two decisions and compute its cyclomatic complexity and basis paths.

tasks.title: Draw the control-flow graph of a 12-line function and mark which statements and branches each of 3 given tests covers
Compute the cyclomatic complexity of a function with loops and conditions and write one test per basis path, then confirm coverage
Design a minimal MC/DC test set for a decision with four conditions and show that a branch-coverage set misses an independent effect

schedule.title: Data flow, mutation and coverage limits
schedule.exercise: Explain why 100 percent statement coverage can coexist with undetected bugs, using one function and its test suite.

tasks.title: List the definitions and uses of each variable in a short function and write tests covering all def-use pairs
Create 10 mutants of a function with simple operator changes, run your tests and compute the mutation score
Take a suite with 100 percent line coverage, find surviving mutants, add assertions to kill them and report the score improvement

schedule.title: Unit and integration testing
schedule.exercise: Choose which dependencies of a payment service to fake, stub or use for real and defend each choice.

tasks.title: Write six parameterised unit tests for a fee calculation function using arrange-act-assert and run them with a test runner
Replace a real SMS gateway with a stub and a spy, test a notification service and verify it sends exactly one message per payment
Spin up a database in a container, write integration tests against it with seeded data and compare their speed and fidelity with mocks

schedule.title: Service and end-to-end testing
schedule.exercise: Write a consumer contract for one API call and say what breaks if the provider renames a field.

tasks.title: Write a consumer contract for a price lookup API and verify a provider stub passes, then rename a field and confirm the check fails
Find the cause of a flaky test that depends on timing, fix it with explicit waiting and run it 50 times without failure
Throttle a test environment to simulate 2G latency and packet loss, run a checkout flow and report which timeouts and retries fail

schedule.title: Test-driven development and legacy code
schedule.exercise: Perform three red-green-refactor cycles on a string calculator kata and record your tests after each cycle.

tasks.title: Implement FizzBuzz by red-green-refactor in six small cycles, committing a failing test before each change
Write property-based tests for a reverse and a sort function with generators and let the tool find a counterexample for a buggy version
Add characterisation tests to an untested 60-line legacy function, then refactor it safely and confirm all tests still pass

schedule.title: Performance testing
schedule.exercise: Describe the workload model for a payment service on salary day, with arrival rate, mix of requests and the target percentiles.

tasks.title: Time 1000 calls to an endpoint stub and report the mean, median, 95th and 99th percentile latency and the error rate
Run load and stress tests with 10, 50 and 200 virtual users and plot throughput against latency to find the saturation point
Fit a queueing model to measured results, predict the capacity needed for a month-end peak and justify the safety margin you choose

schedule.title: Security testing and reporting
schedule.exercise: Pick five test cases from the web testing guide for a login page and describe the expected safe behaviour for each.

tasks.title: Check a sample web app for missing security headers and weak cookie settings and report each finding with its fix
Fuzz a parsing function with 1000 random and mutated inputs, collect the crashing inputs and group them by root cause
Write a combined performance and security findings report for a seeded service and have it scored on severity, evidence and advice

schedule.title: Test management and automation
schedule.exercise: Write entry and exit criteria for a release test and a bug report that a developer can reproduce in one attempt.

tasks.title: Rewrite five poor bug reports with steps, expected and actual results, environment and severity, and have them scored
Build a risk-based test plan for a payments release, rank areas by risk and choose where to spend limited test time
Set up a CI pipeline in the lab VM that runs unit and regression tests on each commit and selects only tests affected by a change

schedule.title: Quality models and metrics
schedule.exercise: Pick three quality characteristics from ISO 25010 for a health app and choose a metric and target for each.

tasks.title: Compute defect density and escaped defect rate for four releases from given data and plot the trend
Fit a reliability growth model to weekly failure counts, estimate remaining failures and decide when testing could stop
Judge a case where speed, security and usability trade off, set quality targets from ISO 25010 and defend them to a board

schedule.title: Process improvement, special testing and capstone
schedule.exercise: Write a quality report for your capstone with coverage, mutation score, defects found and remaining risks.

tasks.title: Calculate deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate and time to restore from a log of 30 releases
Test a currency and date formatting function for Ghanaian cedi and local formats and report the cases where output is wrong
Build a full test suite for a seeded-fault application, find at least eight faults and report coverage, mutation score and residual risk
